text:
Rohan (Finance): FYI SpendSight just sent their renewal offer and an invoice for last month that doesn't match our usage. Renewal is +18% on list. Can someone look at the invoice line items?

Evan (Billing): I saw that. The invoice shows a one-time 'platform surcharge' of $12,500 we never agreed to. Our billing reports show identical token volumes to their exported CSV. I'm flagging a dispute.

Priya (Vendor Ops): Opening a ticket with SpendSight now. Also asked for the original contract reference for that surcharge. @Noah can you hold off on signing the renewal until we get a credit applied?

Noah (Procurement): Holding. On renewal terms — SpendSight proposes a 12mo commit with quarterly true-ups. Competitor ChargeFlow sent a preliminary back-of-envelope that targets 10% lower TCO if we move to their tiered processing model. But migration effort unknown.

Sam (CTO): Two questions: 1) How much effort to switch reconciliation pipeline if we move to ChargeFlow? 2) Are there feature gaps (role-based access, SSO, export retention)? We can run a 30-day pilot but want no data loss and parallel runs.

Rohan (Finance): Quick data ask: can Billing export month-by-month spend and event counts for last 6 months by sku? Need to show committed usage for negotiation. Evan?

Evan (Billing): Will post CSV in #finance-data in 30m. Sample rows:

```
invoice_month,sku,events_processed,storage_gb,amount
2025-01,billable_events,124500,12.3,3120.00
2025-01,storage,12.3,12.3,184.50
```

Evan (Billing): Also attaching reconciliation log where we saw the surcharge applied: surcharge_code=SS-PLATFORM-2025; ledger ref 78a9.

Priya (Vendor Ops): SpendSight replied: surcharge was a "temporary onboarding fee" applied in error and they issued a credit. They uploaded credit_note_1778235000.pdf. Still need to negotiate renewal price.

Rohan (Finance): Great on the credit. For renewal: propose we ask SpendSight for either a 15% discount off list or 9 months at current pricing + 3 months free on a 12mo commit. If they won't budge, start ChargeFlow pilot.

Noah (Procurement): Drafting RFP for both vendors to capture: base fee, per-event fee, storage/egress fees, SLA credits (p99 latency), onboarding/migration credit, API rate limits, data retention, breach notification windows. Will also ask for sample export schema.

legal-bot: Reminder: Request SOC2 Type II report, DPA with export and deletion clauses, subprocessors list, and express indemnity for data breaches. Also request export format (CSV/Parquet) and API versioning guarantees.

Sam (CTO): ChargeFlow offers delta webhooks and claims near-zero replication costs. If true that could save ~15% on our nightly reconciliation job costs. But need to validate payload and schema compatibility.

Priya (Vendor Ops): I scheduled demos: SpendSight on Wed 10am, ChargeFlow on Thu 2pm. I'll invite Billing + Platform + Legal.

Evan (Billing): One more ask: include a line in RFP about historical export replay. If we need to re-ingest 6 months of history, what's the cost and support window?

Noah (Procurement): Noted. Also negotiating leverage: we'll share committed 6mo usage if vendors sign an NDA. I'll attach a sanitized usage table.

Rohan (Finance): Next steps: Evan uploads the 6mo usage CSV (ETA 30m), Noah sends RFP in 48 hours, Priya runs demos, legal-bot to collect compliance docs. Reconvene in 4 days to review vendor responses. /remind me 4 days
